references.text: The principle that the one who sins shall die - each person is responsible for their own sin
A prayer that the wicked be blotted out of the book of life and not written among the righteous
God's book where all days are recorded
Those who are written in the book will be saved
Those enrolled for life in Jerusalem
The promise not to blot the name of the overcomer from the book of life
The judgment by the book of life - those not written in it are cast into the lake of fire
Only those written in the Lamb's book of life may enter the new Jerusalem
Paul's coworkers have their names in the book of life
Moses asks that God either forgive the people's sin or blot his name from the book - the immediate context
Direct quotation and theological foundation: Romans confirms God's sovereign right to choose who remains in the book.
Narrative and theological parallel: Restoration of the tablets (the covenant) after the sin in chapter 32, while the individual sinner is blotted out.
